Max Verstappen won from pole for Red Bull, finishing 7.335 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc, who took second and the fastest lap for Ferrari, with Andrea Kimi Antonelli third for Mercedes. The classification shows a clean conversion of a front-row start into a win, George Russell climbing from nineteenth to ninth and Isack Hadjar from twenty-second to tenth for a point, while four cars retired: Alexander Albon, Lance Stroll, Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto.
highlights: Isack Hadjar made the biggest climb of the race, moving from twenty-second on the grid to finish tenth and score a point.
Charles Leclerc took the fastest lap while finishing second for Ferrari, 7.335 seconds behind winner Max Verstappen.
Four cars retired without finishing: Alexander Albon, Lance Stroll, Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto.

review.summary: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia in round 17, ahead of Jorge Martin; Raul Fernandez took third for SuperFile Trackhouse. Aprilia dominated the front with three of the top four finishers, while Yamaha's Razgatlioglu and Miller, along with Bagnaia and Aldeguer, did not finish.
highlights: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia for Aprilia Racing.
Raul Fernandez finished second for SuperFile Trackhouse and Jorge Martin third for Aprilia Racing.
Toprak Razgatlioglu, Jack Miller, Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer did not finish.

review.summary: Taylor Barnard of DS Penske won from sixth on the grid, ahead of Mahindra Racing's Nyck De Vries, who started on pole and finished second, and team-mate Edoardo Mortara third from grid two. Sébastien Buemi climbed to fifth after starting tenth. Front-row cars Pascal Wehrlein (grid three) and Nico Müller (grid four) faded to 14th and 12th, while Joel Eriksson and Lucas Di Grassi did not finish.
highlights: Norman Nato started nineteenth and finished tenth for Nissan, climbing nine places to score a single point.
Oliver Rowland started seventeenth on the grid and finished ninth for Nissan, eight places up to score three points.
Nyck De Vries began on pole for Mahindra Racing but finished second behind winner Taylor Barnard, with team-mate Edoardo Mortara third.
Front-row cars Pascal Wehrlein and Nico Müller faded to fourteenth and twelfth after starting third and fourth for Porsche.
